title: Water conservation measures amid Mannheim supply constraint
subtitle: Bylaw review, expanded audit programs, working group reporting, and a short-term Mannheim growth forecast.
overview: Regional Council held a special meeting on water. Council endorsed expanding the Region's existing industrial, commercial, institutional and residential conservation programs starting in 2027 {{vote:m5}}. It also directed a consultant-assisted review of the Water Conservation Bylaw, with public consultation, to decide whether intermediate steps are needed before a full watering ban {{vote:m6}}.

The Water Conservation Working Group will keep meeting and report to Council at least twice a year {{vote:m3}}. Staff said an outdoor watering ban is not immediately needed but should be ready on standby. Staff were also directed to report back on re-establishing the Water Efficiency Advisory Committee.

Council also received a short-term growth forecast for the Mannheim Service Area. It expects most of the Region's growth over the next five years, though overall growth is slower than in the past decade. Staff were asked to return with more detailed assessments of population and economic growth by area municipality. These items had no separate motions. The closed session on an internal review of the Mannheim water constraint had no public outcome in the minutes.
For residents, this means more water-saving audits and incentives, a possible bylaw change after consultation, and continued public reporting.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed expanding the Region's industrial, commercial, institutional and residential conservation programs from 2027, with more communication and collaboration with area municipalities.
Council directed a consultant-assisted review of the bylaw to see whether intermediate steps are needed before a full watering ban, with public consultation before any changes return to Council.
Council directed the Water Conservation Working Group to keep meeting and report at least semi-annually on mid- and long-term conservation policies and programs.
Council amended a proposed quarterly reporting schedule to semi-annual or more frequent reports as necessary {{vote:m4}}.

debate: A delegate said the report did not go far enough and urged seasonal water pricing and review of minimum-usage billing. One councillor responded that higher water costs could hurt residents already struggling to pay bills and taxes.

The consultant said pricing changes fall under area municipalities, need careful rate modelling, and are not feasible for this summer. A regulatory option such as a watering ban would be the quicker tool, but it is not currently needed.

Some councillors said they were disappointed the recommendations focused on short-term savings rather than water-efficient new development. Staff said the work targeted quick savings and that grey water and rainwater systems are still costly and slow to take hold.

On the working group, the mover wanted quarterly reports because of the urgency and the value of building efficiency into new buildings. Staff said quarterly reports would have little new to say, which led to the semi-annual compromise.

One councillor questioned the use of consultants and suggested delaying the bylaw review until staff are less busy. Another asked for stronger accountability on expected savings from added program funding.
